Target: Community Based Surveillance (CBS) is a system that relies on reporting a suspected case or the trend of a specific disease(s) using a community case definition. A community case definition is two or three easily identified symptoms associated with a specific disease. It is a more basic form of syndromic (symptom) reporting that is used by health professionals in national/IDSR and other disease surveillance systems. [TG_Booklet_1:p436-p441:c0087]

Members of the Village Health Committee (VHC) should receive training in all aspects of surveillance and response, including how to recognize certain diseases or health conditions for the purpose of reporting suspect cases. They should also be trained in improved interpersonal skills using interactive training, adult learning techniques, and role playing. Additionally, training should include the use of picture-based and game-based job aids, as well as cell-phone based opportunities to play MP3s or other video clips. For literate VHCs, simple alert forms should be designed and shown how to fill information, while for non-literate VHCs, mechanisms should be developed to capture information of events from them, such as identifying a family member to assist with actual writing.
